utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Brennskag.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karadzic. I hope your biorhythm is okay on Monday morning. Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. Dr. Karadzic would like to address you this morning concerning our schedule for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to everyone. I'd like to say that I don't have a single day off, because I'm spending all my time in preparation. I don't have any time for strolling outdoors or for sports activity. But that aside, I don't have sufficient time for preparations, themselves. Therefore, I asked Mr. Robinson to send a letter in which we would request for a day off tomorrow to give me some respite and to allow me to prepare for the next witness. Let's disregard my need for sports activities and rest, but I must say that I'm not ready to continue at this pace without any breaks. I'm afraid that I didn't say that I'm not ready to continue, I just said that I don't have any breaks or any respite. Of course, I am interested in having this finalised as soon as possible so that I can go home. I want these proceedings to finish quickly, but this will result in a bad Defence case, and, secondly, this can jeopardise my health condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To be sure, could you kindly remind me, Mr. Tieger, of the order of witnesses after this. I take it the first witness would be Ms. Mujanovic, and the next one will be Dr. Hajir?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Both of them are supposed to be heard via videolink?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the videolink installation has been prepared for today and tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct. And then we have -- in anticipation of concluding the videolink testimony, or at least approaching a conclusion of the videolink testimony, we have the testimony of KDZ323 following.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Followed by KDZ244, and then 485.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that we are sitting for an extended time today, I propose to adjourn today or tomorrow when we will have finished those two witnesses that are to be heard via videolink. In case we are going to finish early tomorrow morning, we'll see to it that Mr. Karadzic can go back to Scheveningen as early as possible, but I think we may be able to finish those two witnesses this afternoon. We'll see. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to just raise with the Court the possible knock-on effect with respect to this week's schedule, and concluding one witness in particular. And if I might go into private session for a moment to address that. You're right, that's -- perhaps I can address it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us finish this --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's fine, I understand, but I think it's important to raise that issue. [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- I'll hear from you. Sorry for the inconvenience, Mr. Brennskag. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think that after we have finished with the videolink witnesses, I accept your proposal. It is feasible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On Friday, we talked about what you knew about the offensive of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in July. You said that there was -- that you didn't know of any such offensive; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time in June/July 1995, the situation for the UN observers were very difficult. UN observers on the BSA side were detained by the BSA, and we, who were trying to do our job inside Sarajevo, had very much limitations. At that time, I didn't know any exact movements of any of the factions. In my notes that I think I was writing in 2001, I tried to find out what had happened, and then I collected some information. But at that time in 1995, I didn't know any exact movements of any troops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Karadzic. I should have noted that we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Judge Lattanzi will not be with us during the morning today. She'll be joining us in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This amalgamated statement of yours was updated on the 13th and 14th of October, 2010; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The amalgamated statement, yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please focus on paragraph 31. Why didn't you mention this paragraph, that there was a major Muslim Army offensive -- or, rather, Army of B and H, in Bosnia -- in Sarajevo and in Bosnia, as a whole: [In English] "In June 1995 it was a very hectic time. There could be up to 150 impacts coming into Sarajevo during a 24-hour period."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Brennskag, would you like to see your statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just about to give you -- the exhibit number is P1851.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I believe the witness has already answered why there was no reference to Muslim or BH offensives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but this question can be viewed from a somewhat different perspective. But do you, by any chance, have a hard copy of his statement? Now we have it. The previous page, para 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question was: If you didn't know then and if you learned about that later, why didn't you, in October of this year, mention that there was a major offensive? Why I'm asking you this: Your words are being taken very seriously here, but you said: [In English] "But mostly it could be up to 150. These 150 rounds were hitting both civilians and military targets." [Interpretation] And so on and so forth. Can you see this paragraph, and don't you think that it would only be fair and truthful if you had mentioned here that a major offensive had been launched by the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said for some minutes ago, this was second-hand information that I was collecting a long time after the Balkan war, around 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this paragraph 31 is full of assertions that can serve as a basis for a guilty verdict. You say that they were targeting non-military targets, and then you go on to say that after you and your service had investigated these matters, you concluded that those were purely civilian targets that were wounded or died. Do you believe that things changed if you put it into the context of a major Muslim offensive in which not 120, but 2.000 or 3.000 shells were fired from the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have stated that, as far as I remember, it could be around 150 rounds hitting both civilian and military targets at that time, but some of them, what we were observing at this time, were purely landing or impacting in civilian areas. What -- why I conclude on that is about the investigation on the impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brennskag, judging by this paragraph only, an image is created of the town being terrorised, of civilian targets being hit, and a huge number of shells being fired at Sarajevo. All of that was the other around. You didn't know that at the time, but you knew that in 2002. Why didn't you include, in your 2010 statement, the information that all of that took place as part of the most important major offensive launched by the Muslim Army?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all respect, I testify what I was observing in June/July 1995. I'm sorry that we couldn't observe impacts from firing out of BiH side, and we did not have any observers on the BSA side; they were detained by BSA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I to take it, then, that your testimony and your knowledge are limited and fragmented?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: My knowledge is what I have stated in my testimony. And if it's fragmented, I don't think, for myself, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you then trying to say that you have a comprehensive knowledge and that you're telling the whole truth with relation to the events that you observed in your capacity of an observer?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a UN observer, I was just a small part of a big UN operation that tried to put together what was happening during that time. I was just a small part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But then we have to conclude that what you are telling us here is only a shred of truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brennskag, you say that at that time, you didn't know that there was an offensive going on and that you didn't know how many shells fell on each side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I didn't know -- I hadn't any exact information about offensives going on, and, in fact, my job was not depending on this information. I only reported what I saw when I was on the job, the impacts inside Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know - or perhaps you didn't know - that the Muslim Army had launched a major offensive in order to make a breakthrough from Sarajevo? Did you know about that or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at your notes, page 10. In the meantime, can we look at 65 ter 14332. While we're waiting for this document: Sir, is it correct that you conveyed your information and your observation to your command, and that it was at your command where comprehensive reports were being compiled?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll answer the last question. It's correct that my information and reports were delivered or given to the UN Observer HQ in Sarajevo or normally through my team leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the one who compiled this comprehensive information in the UNMO service were doing so based on second-hand information, that is to say, the information that you provided?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The UNMO -- UN -- UNMO HQ in Sarajevo, they obtained their information through the UNMO teams that were operating, and at that time they were just operating on the BiH side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. So those at the HQ did not need to have direct knowledge of an eye-witness, but they, rather, used information received from teams; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The UNMO teams were the UN Observer HQ's eyes and ears during that time, and the reports about events were given through the UN teams, either written in reports or orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were not at your observation post and you observed something, would you send a report on that as well?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be done through the team leader, normally, or sometimes also when we were patrolling, we went directly to the UNMO HQ in Sarajevo, PTT building, and reported orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please answer with a yes or no. So in addition to observation posts, you carry out your duties by patrolling; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my time when I was not assigned to the OP, we had some patrolling, but it was very limited because we were put restrictions on us from the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you to please look at the last paragraph, which starts "UNMO Sarajevo ..." Do you agree that your observers did not have full insight and that there were unconfirmed reports to the effect that the BH Army made some territorial advances on the 16th of June? The last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read the last paragraph. Again, this is from my notes in 2001, and this is what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Can the witness be shown the full document, please? Can we zoom out so the witness can see the full document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, I'm sorry. Could I then see the last paragraph again?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sorry, just one thing. Okay, look at the paragraph which is last --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having read the title of this document, do you like to correct your statement, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is from -- a report from UNMO HQ. Could I have the whole document again, please. Daily sitrep, yes, and I have no more information about this sitrep than what is written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: From this document, one can gather that the "UNMO Sarajevo" was about the situation, in particular the Muslim offensive, although they didn't know the result of that offensive in detail. Was such kind of information not conveyed to UNMO teams in the field by those UNMO Sarajevo headquarter? I'm referring to the ABiH operation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very limited about the information we got from the UNMO HQ. Sometimes maybe the team leaders got some information from the HQ, and sometimes we didn't get this information further. I don't recall that this information from this daily sitrep, that I got it from the UNMO HQ or from my team leader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, who informed whom? Were you reporting to the HQ or was the HQ reporting to you?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally, the observation teams reported to the UNMO HQ inside Sarajevo. Information -- generally, information to us were received through, normally, our team leader from UNMO HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were OP 4; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in OP 4 several times, yes. Normally, 24 hours per time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why did you say that that observation post was called Sierra Victor 2?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The UNMO HQ or the UNMO Sarajevo had abbreviations for the OPs, and as far as I remember, it should be "Sierra Whiskey 2," because I think, or remember that the "Sierra" stands for "Sarajevo," and "Whiskey" stands for "West," and "2," "Number 2."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But Mr. Brennskag, "Sierra" were the names of check-points, not observation points; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. UNMO HQ or UNMO Sarajevo did never have any check-points. We had observation posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will see how that is marked. Can we look at page 11 of this document, please, so that we can see what OP 4 knew and reported back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. It was last week, Mr. Brennskag - it's at page 8666, line 4 to 6 - and to the question: "What were your observation posts known as," you did answer: "I can only remember exactly my own observation post, and this was on the hills of Vitkovac, and as far as I remember, it was called Sierra Victor 2." Was it a mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was Sierra Whiskey 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to look at what was reported from that station at 1447. That the Bosnian side fired; is that correct? "4" -- I don't know the abbreviation. Is that correct? This is the fourth line from the top.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the line. At the time, "1447 Bravo" means local time. It means OP 4, my OP, but I have to state that I don't know if I was at the OP 4 at that time. And it explains that the four explosions landing in Stup area, it's a map grid, Bravo Papa 8457. It means that it's not more accurate than 1 K square fired from. They don't state, and that's why this is unknown and "Fired BiH."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to move faster, allow me to present this page, and you can follow. So at 1450, somebody fired at the Spicasta Stijena, and then at 1500 hours -- actually, at 1650, there was a strike. At 1500 -- at 1650, there was a strike. At 15, somebody fired at Hrasno, and then so on and so forth, all the way up to 1510 hours, when the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina fired again, and so on and so forth. Is that correct? Is this a minute-by-minute report, and is this a battle with artillery fire being exchanged?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I tried to explain, I don't think I was at the OP at this time. I think this is a report from the 16th of June. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I think that this is a report dated the 17th, covering the 16th of July [as interpreted]. But, Mr. Brennskag, this is the usual report by your Military Observers service; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a daily report, yes, from UNMO HQ in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it is reporting on what it received from OP 4 and so on and so forth, OP 1 and so on and so forth. And now, Mr. Brennskag, do you see that your service was completely aware of a major offensive and exchange of fire? If you look at 1620, 1617, and so on -- can we look at the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we move on: Mr. Brennskag, the last column represents, I take it, remarks. There, we see "Fired BiH" or "Fired BSA." What does it mean? Does it mean BiH was fired or it is BiH that fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The last column is stating who was firing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We can see that we've got the "BiH outgoing," "BSA fired," "BiH outgoing." From minute to minute, the exchange of fire is being recorded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the report that came from -- that was received from the OPs, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see, in the first paragraph, "Other Significant/Relevant Information," that the B and H Army took your observation post at Mojmilo, which was held by the Russians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read what's in the report. I don't think this is a UN observer -- a UN observation post. It's stated that it's held by the Russians, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were the Russians part of the United Nations or were they there as part of the Russian Army? "UN OP," that's what it says on the first line.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but as it's stated that it was held by the Russians, UN Russians were there as UNPROFOR or UNP, and they had their own observation posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see in the next paragraph, the first sentence: "Sector OPS Sarajevo --" [In English] "... believe the ABiH have made territorial gains in the area ..." [Interpretation] Is it possible to capture territory by means of defensive tactics or by means of an offensive?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's stated that the BiH, they took the OP, and that must have been done by an attack or a movement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. The whole document is of interest and it's instructive and I would like to tender it. I cannot spend any more time with you on the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D850, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Once again, I must ask you: Were the United Nations aware of the major offensive that the Muslim Army launched on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that United Nations troops or organisation knew about the offensive, yes, but I didn't know then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Again, this was a useless question. The witness said that he didn't know at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then look at 65 ter 8186, please. This is, again, a daily sitrep of your UNMO service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brennskag, you are talking about things in a pretty general way. You're not talking about things that you, yourself, saw with your own eyes, but about broader events, so let's see what your service was aware of. Let's look at all the things that your service was aware of.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This has been admitted as Exhibit P1860.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a report of the 19th of June, 1995. Can we now look at the following page. Do you agree that in the first paragraph, it says that the offensive of the B and H Army is expected to continue? Can you look at the first paragraph: "The situation remains extremely tense and limited ..." [In English] "... ABiH offensive is expected to continue." [Interpretation] Limited to Sarajevo, thus; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen this report before, I think. And I read the same as you, but I have -- we were not the recipients of these kind of reports. So, again, I just read what is stated in the report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And let's see what your OP reported back. Can we look at the fifth page on from this one. It says "086180." Actually, we need the following page, the ERN number. But here also you have that there was fire at Nedzarici, which is a Serbian neighbourhood, and then on this page also you can see OP 4 is reporting that the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army and the Army of Republika Srpska fired, and more shots were fired by the Bosnia-Herzegovina Army. And then SC-1 reports, and so on and so forth. Is that correct.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I again see the report, and I can state what I've stated before: At that time, it was a lot of firing outgoing from Sarajevo and incoming into Sarajevo, and I'm not sure that I was on the OP when those reports was given to -- were given to the UNMO HQ. But it was a very hectic time, firing from both sides of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And let's just look at the next page quickly. It's the same kind of thing, a minute-by-minute report on the situation for that day?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, which page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next page. Yes, 182 is the ERN number, and you can see that the exchange of fire was being recorded from minute to minute, and you can see that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was not lagging behind in any way in this firing. Can we look at the next page, please. And then can we look at 185, the ERN number, the last digits of the ERN number. This is page 12 of a total of 16 pages of this document. And you can see here: [In English] "UNMO Team SW-2 carried out investigation ..." [Interpretation] It seems that there was an investigation carried out into a 120-millimetre mortar strike. It was difficult to confirm -- it was not possible to confirm or establish the location because the local police removed the fragments, and the impact site was into a concrete wall four metres above ground level, and so on and so forth. Do you see this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you were taken to the morgue to see some seven bodies. How do you know where those bodies came from?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I have to say that I was not investigating this incident myself, so I have no answer to the question because I was not at the spot and I was not at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But in your statements, you give a general assessment, a general picture of the situation, and this is a document of your service. Can you please look at the last sentence on this page: "About the military situation for the BSA at the moment, he said that the BiH had launched several offensives and attacks ..." [In English] " ... in the last days, but that the BSA had no problems holding their positions." [Interpretation] Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure -- you say my statement gave a general assessment, a general picture of the situation. Is that from my private document from 2001?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it Mr. Karadzic was referring to the last paragraph of this document, not yours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. This is an assessment of the UNMO HQ and not my assessment, so I read what it stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In relation to this document, you stated in your amalgamated statement -- in para 33, you stated that you were not sure if you were on that observation post that day. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said, Mr. Brennskag, that the Muslim side had only mortars, and you noted one tank, for which you say that you didn't see when it fired, you didn't see it firing?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said that I saw -- I knew about mortars, and I saw the single tank just beside or on my way to OP 4. I didn't see it was firing. I did not say that I knew about -- exactly about the other weapons the ABiH had.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at 1D2567 now, please. I'm afraid there is no translation, but I will read it to you, and I kindly ask the interpreters to control whether -- actually, I'm going to read in the Serbian, and the interpreters will translate. This is -- I'm going to read slowly to allow the interpreters to keep up, and they have the document on the screen. This is a strictly confidential order by the commander of the 12th Division. It's an order to attack of the 11th of June, 1995. Plan T -- Plan Tekbir thus approved by the commander of the 1st Corps Brigade, General Karavelic, and in the first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Brennskag said he didn't know that there was a Muslim offensive in those days. Is it an appropriate use of time to put such document to this witness? Do you think this witness is in the position to confirm or not about this document? You can use this with another witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I'm not tendering the document in order to confirm whether there was an offensive or not but in order to look at the positions of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina which the observers should have known about. Exactly in front of the OP 4 observation post were the command posts and the artillery positions of the army, which should have been observed. So if you allow me to move to the next page so that we can see what this looks like. Can we look at the next page, please. Allow me to read the last sentence in the first paragraph: "The units are of good morale, and they are -- are of good morale and are manned up to the strength of 80 per cent in manpower and up to 120 per cent in materiel and equipment." And if you can look at the "12th Division," I'm going to read to you the assignment: "At the beginning of assault actions in the areas of the 14th and the 16th Division, in joint co-ordination with units of the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP ..." But we will skip that as well. Can we look at the next page so that we can see where the command post and the artillery positions were. They were right in front of you. Here it is. We're reading 5.1: "Supported by the division -- the 12th Artillery Group ..." We are reading at the end of this 5.1: "Supported by the Artillery Group 12, command post in the sector of Astra, forward command post in the sector of the Sokolje village." And all of these were around your posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Astra is located right next to the television building?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: About Astra, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at paragraph 5.3. It says: "Supported by DH 12," that's the Artillery Battalion Group 12: "Command post in the sector of Blagoje Parovic School and forward command post in the sector of Orlici." That was left of your observation post; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I have stated that I knew there were mortars positioned close to or downhill from the OP.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down a bit to see where the command post of the 105 Mountain Brigade was. It's in the area of the park. So when the Serbs fire at the park, the reports come out of them firing at a civilian zone. Can you scroll down a bit. A little bit more, please. It's all right now. It says here: "BBR 152, supported by the DAG-12 command post in the Park Sector, a forward command post in the compound of Kosevo Hospital under construction." Did you know that in the compound of the Kosevo Hospital, there were artillery, there were command posts?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier, I have stated that at that time the UN observers inside Sarajevo had a very strict -- correct -- they were very restricted where to go, and we were never allowed to go towards the confrontation line or to the parts where we could expect to find troops or weapons. The restrictions came from ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With all due respect, Mr. Brennskag, you cannot then say that it was the Serbs who fired at civilian targets. Look at what it says about the 152 Brigade: "Command post in the Prkos Sector, forward command post in the Vratnik Sector."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You should not make a statement which is not answered. Mr. Brennskag, Mr. Karadzic said: "You cannot then say that it was the Serbs who fired at civilian targets." Do you like to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I have only stated that those investigations I had been doing was fired and hurting or killing civilians. That's a special -- it was the 22nd of July, especially that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we just briefly go through the next page so that we can see where the 115th Brigade is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 115 Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The command post is on the 6th of April Square. Can we look at the next page now. Look at 5.9. I think we have to go one page back. 5.9: "Command post of 155th Brigade is in Dobrinja 2 Sector, and 102nd is in the area of wire factory." And below that: "The 12th --" Can you please scroll down.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the accused please repeat the last statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the wire factory was located between your command post and the TV building? Did you know where this facility was?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about the wire factory. There were a lot of factory buildings, but we didn't know what they contained or what they have been used for.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll up this page altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the Hum Hill is? Scroll down, not up.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I know where the Hum Hill is. It's where the radio and television antenna were situated. I were never up at this hill, but I was just downside Mali Hum, where one colleague observer team had their accommodation and OP, observation post, in the same building; Mali Hum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The last sentence says: "The command post of the 12th Artillery Battalion in Velesici, and its forward command post in the Hum Sector." Can we look at the next page now. Please look at item 7. I'm going to read it out to you. We are talking about anti-armour combat, Velesici Sector, command post of a rocket battery, Mojmilo, and then the task implies that they have a TF-B launcher, that they have a tank platoon, then they have: "POR in the Ciglana Sector (tunnel)." Then they have: "POP-1 in the Brijesca Brda Sector." And we are going to show all these locations in the map, which is where you had your observation posts: "POP-2 in Buce Sector. "POP-3 in Sedrenik Sector. "POP-4 in Stup Sector." And: "POP-5 in Donji Velesici Sector." Would it only be logical to expect that UNMOs were aware of these deployments if we are to rely on their reports?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only say what I, myself, know, and I didn't exactly know any of these positions and I was not allowed to go there on patrol.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we move two pages ahead to see how they managed to conceal that and why you were kept in the dark. Now I need page 8. I'm going to read to you as follows. That's the fourth bullet from the top, which reads: "Establish special regime of traffic, with maximum possible control of vehicles and persons, particularly UNPF and UNMO and other international organisations. If necessary, close off all the entry and exit points to and from Sarajevo for UNPF and other international associations. All representatives of international institutions shall be banned from entering the zone of combat operations without special consent by the commander of the 12th Division of the Land Army. Prevent the withdrawal of UNPF and, if necessary, bring it into encirclement." Then it says: "Fully ensure and protect artillery weapons from video and photographing by unauthorised persons." Now, do I have to repeat anything for the benefit of the transcript? So it seems that you were treated there as a hostile army. They made sure that you didn't see anything and you didn't know anything. And at that time when they are launching their major offensive, they are hiding their weapons, whereas when we respond, we are accused of firing at civilian areas. Were you able -- was your service capable of portraying a full picture of what was going on? You said you didn't. Could you confirm that the Serbs were the ones who fired at civilians?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I have to answer the first question about the picture, what's going on. I have stated that at that time we had big problems to do our work inside Sarajevo, and we had no observers on the BSA side. The problems that were created to know what was going on inside Sarajevo was the restriction put on us by the ABiH. Then I was asked a question about if it only was the Serbs who fired at civilians. What I only know is what I was investigating and what I was seeing about the incoming improvised air-bombs, and some of them, especially the one I was investigating, was landing and killing civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that, Mr. Brennskag. Did you ever see any casualty on the spot?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw one casualty on the spot on the 22nd of June -- of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you moving from this document, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I'd like to have it tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was waiting, Mr. Karadzic. I warned you that it may not be an efficient way of using time. It took eight pages, in terms of transcript, and you spent 25 hours [sic] despite my -- I'm sorry, 25 minutes. You're reading out these documents or your questions that do not form part of the evidence. That's the sort of advice you should get from your legal advisers. The witness did not confirm anything about this document, and there's no basis for us to admit this document through this witness. Just seriously consider the advice given from the Chamber. You could have asked the witness whether he knew the deployment of BiH forces. That could have been done in one or two minutes. You didn't have to put all these questions to the witness. Bear that in mind, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Your Excellency, all of that was done for the next document, which is a map. And I studied the testimony of this witness in other trials, and I know how much attention was given to his testimony, irrespective of the fact that UNMO reports were useless. Now, in order to prove that I had my reasons for asking these questions, I would like to call up P1853. The things that the observers didn't know, what they should have known, disqualifies it entirely as a service. Now, can we have, please, P1853.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would note that that last remark by the accused was entirely argumentative and didn't address the Court's question at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, Mr. Brennskag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, refrain from making statements. Yes, what is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is: Did you know that high-ranking UNPROFOR officers considered UNMO's reports inaccurate, unreliable, and unusable? Did you know or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: This the first time I've heard this accusation, and, no, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this map show your observation post?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the triangle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To the right or to the west of your observation post, can you see the feature called "Brijesko Brdo"?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the name on the map, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to put a circle around "Brijesko Brdo." Well, you needn't do that. Suffice it that you identified it. Now, can you see "Boljakov Potok" to the east of your post?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the name written in letters, yes, "Boljakov Potok."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the bottom right-hand corner, do you see that it's written "Tvornica Zice," a wire factory. Next to the railway tracks, to the south of the railway tracks, it says "AMK Tvornica Zice"?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read "AMK Tvornica Zice," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see the radio and television building, painted red?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. East of the "RTV," it says "Gras." That's the Sarajevo public transport company and all its assets and installations. Mr. Brennskag, I am listing the localities where crucial military installations of the BH Army were deployed, artillery positions and displacement and other positions. Do you -- or did you know that the BH Army installations were clustered all around you? Those are the ones that we listed in the previous document which at the time seemed to be irrelevant. Now you see "Kuca Potok," "Donji Dolac," et cetera. These are all the localities occupied by the BH Army and from which they threatened us. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the positions or the names on the map. We were restricted to go and see what was there. And I didn't know then that it was army locations, and I don't know now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But from a BH Army document, we saw that those were important places where they had command posts and artillery and mortar positions from which they opened fire. If your evidence is to be ascribed considerable credibility, then you should have known that.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I didn't because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's not for the witness. The witness said he didn't know that. You should move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has this document been admitted? Yes, it's a P exhibit, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Brennskag, can you tell me this: The so-called aerial bomb that you saw hitting the TV building, had it flown over your observation post?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was observed in front of the observation post, and I have to state that this is the 28th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd rather think it was June, it was not July. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we remove this map and show a photograph, D808, Exhibit D808.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this projectile capable of flying over the position where Captain Hansen was? Can you see your observation post in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not my observation post.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar with this area?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I could see the television building in the middle of the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the other buildings, the wire factory, in the background? Can you see other facilities?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know it was a wire factory. I see a building behind the TV building, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, you had never seen an aerial bomb before it's being fired?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But before it was fired, did you see this bomb before it was fired, before it would be fired?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never seen a modified air-bomb before it was fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated that -- your testimony in the case of General Milosevic on the 8th of March, on page 3467, did you state that in your opinion, mortars were more precise in comparison with the air-bombs?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in a way that the mortars, they are able to hit the target, and you can correct the impact so you will have the effect that you want.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am looking at the time, and I'm just wondering whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me, sir, Mr. Brennskag, you stated that you were not educated -- you did not have education or information about how these modified air-bombs were launched; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no previous education about modified air-bombs, no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break for half an hour. We'll resume at 11.00. {The witness stands down]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I appreciated the Chamber's suggestion to raise the matter after the conclusion of this witness's testimony, but as I indicated, there may be some knock-on effects and time may be of the essence in certain respects. I'd like to raise one specific matter in private session and then move on to some more general comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. More generally -- and I appreciate the opportunity to be heard with respect -- in private session with respect to that specific matter, but more generally, I wanted to once again raise the point that changes in the court schedule on short notice clearly have an impact on witness schedules and on the witnesses, themselves, and, for that reason, among others, have to be balanced against the basis of the request and the rights of the accused. In this particular case, we've heard submissions this morning, also the message by e-mail from Mr. Robinson earlier, the documents in question are 66(B) requests, that is, responses to the accused's broad request for a wide range of information produced by witnesses, most of which, if not all of which, have little to do with the specific nature of the -- and specific focus of the witnesses' testimony and, in any event, are amenable to rapid review to determine whether or not they are of assistance to the accused. The other factor, of course, was the witness interview. All of these factors, I would emphasise, bear on the accused's decision to assume for himself virtually all, if not all, of the responsibilities associated with presenting the case. Now, he certainly has a right to self-representation and a right to do that, but there are concomitant responsibilities that go with that, including accepting the inevitable consequences of not delegating to others such responsibilities as interviewing witnesses before they appear in court. So I raise that because the effect on this schedule is that -- for this week, is that clearly not all the witnesses who were scheduled to be called can be called, and I raised it at this point before Mr. Brennskag concluded because it may be possible to prevent one witness from -- who's scheduled to travel today from travelling, if it is, indeed, the Court's intention to block out tomorrow instead of hearing testimony on that date. But as a general matter, I did want to express concern about the impact of the accused's decision to take onto himself every aspect of trial presentation and trial preparation. That would certainly not normally be the approach taken by a trial team. That may be his decision, but it shouldn't mean that witnesses suffer for it. But, again, I raise the matter now because, depending on the Court's decision, there still may be an opportunity for us to take some ameliorative steps. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we know, Mr. Tieger, when were those materials requested for by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There's been a standing request for those materials for quite some time, and the accused and the Defence team is well aware of the fact that we have to prioritise the allocation of resources to undertake those searches, in accordance with all the other responsibilities that the Prosecution has. So they're well aware of the fact that they're provided on a rolling basis. That has been the case ever since late June, and we continue to move forward on those at the earliest possible opportunity, balancing those against all the other responsibilities and burdens and necessary resource limitations that exist, including responding periodically to very specific requests for assistance by the Defence, with which we always attempt to accommodate them if it is at all possible. So I think that the more -- I believe the more significant point at this moment is: What is the nature of the review necessary, in light of those documents which don't have to do with the specific incidents involved, but -- and can be reviewed very quickly to determine whether or not they fall within the province of whatever it is that the Defence considered they might possibly be useful for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. I looked at the trial schedule again, and in my estimate, we may be able to finish the evidence of those two witnesses via videolink at the end of today; at most, the early part of tomorrow morning. Then you'll have the whole of tomorrow morning. And Wednesday, we are sitting in the afternoon, so I take it we should be able to hear the evidence of KDZ485 on Wednesday afternoon. Is that an impossibility, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First, let me say we are preparing for witnesses in the sequence announced to us by the OTP. Secondly, the OTP often changes something. With all due respect to Mr. Tieger, I think the time is not the most important aspect, but the aspect of establishing the truth is. This is not a gun-fight. We need to have enough time at our disposal. I understand why miners work in two or three shifts. They want to earn some money. What can I earn from such a rhythm where I cannot even lift my head from so much work? From what I have heard in other Defence teams, even good lawyers were not able, in the time allotted, to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having heard the situation in which the witness is in, so I'm just exploring the possibility to accommodate his request as much as possible. So I take it your answer is no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, because my team in Belgrade is preparing, and it should be coming. They are preparing for that particular witness, and in the meantime I have one witness before that. That is KDZ --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have two witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have two. But 485, nobody's preparing for him at this point in time, because I have two before that, 323 and 244.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In that case, I would like to recommend you, Mr. Tieger, to consider this, consider to swap the order of witnesses, either the order of KDZ485 with either of those two witnesses who are to be coming before him, in consultation with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Will do, Your Honour, and that's one of the reasons I raised it right now. It appears to me at this point that the testimony of KDZ244 cannot be accommodated this week, under the circumstances described by the Court. And if that's the case, I can see no reason at all why we couldn't accommodate the specific circumstances that the Court just alluded to and make sure we hear a witness who needs to be heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we had requested eight hours for KDZ485, not the 14 that I mentioned. I'm sure you'll be happy to hear that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, we are, Mr. Robinson. And I take it we'll be able to finish this witness's evidence during this session, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so, Your Excellency, because the witness has a very selective memory and his statement has been admitted in previous cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger. Sorry, Your Honour. Just reverting to the scheduling issue quickly. One of the factors I didn't mention, but the Court will be aware of it, is that at least two of the witnesses scheduled for next week are fixed, and so that gives us much less flexibility to bleed over, which is one of the reasons I mentioned the inability to accommodate the testimony of one of the witnesses this week. So it will turn out to be a matter of significant rescheduling, rather than simply moving forward progressively. But I think we can do that, and I will alert the Court if there's any difficulty with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brennskag, we are now dealing with the incident of the 28th of June, 1995, involving the bombing of the television building. You said that you saw the place from where the projectile was fired; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the place from where it was fired.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 13567, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And while we are waiting: Can you describe exactly what you saw at the moment of firing.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could I please have the English written version. At first, I saw a smoke projectile, and you could follow the smoke tail from where it was fired. And, of course, you hear the explosion, or afterwards. First, you see the smoke tail of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. At that point in time, you were at OP 4; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was when I was in OP 4 early in the morning the 28th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I please ask you to look at this map in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we not have a map of better quality? It should be page 8 of the Sarajevo-specific court binder.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, page 8, but we need a map without detail. We need to mark it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Usually when we zoom in, we should be able to see the detail. But in this case, it's impossible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to see if Mr. Brennskag can find his way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see Vitkovac here?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to see on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we really do need a better map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can this map be better?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm able to find approximately where my OP was on this map, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, to mark that place with the number 1? Can you mark it with a triangle, circle, and the number 1.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll try, but it will be approximately because the map is not that good.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I think the map's being switched. A better-quality map is being up-loaded now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you wait until a nicer map is up-loaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Until then, Mr. Brennskag, how about this: Did you observe that point before the firing? What was it that attracted your attention?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: My attention was attracted of the smoke in the air, and I was able to trace the smoke back to from where it was firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So first of all you saw smoke at the point of the origination of the fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you followed. So at the moment of firing, your attention was drawn by smoke; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my attention at the smoke path directly in front of me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For how long did you follow that smoke trail?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to remember, but let's say half of the path. But that's just an assumption today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How long did that take, in terms of time?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you able to mark Vitkovac on this map? Can we zoom in on the left half. Oh, we cannot, because then we will lose the whole map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did he mark anything? We can zoom in.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Further, we can zoom in further. Would this be fine, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see Vitkovac here, where it says -- east of number 5, just below the line marking this rectangle?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the name "Vitkovac" on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please -- or, rather, do you see where the TV is, number 17?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Why don't we zoom in further. Usher, could you come back again. Let's do it after zooming in further. Yes, and go up. Up, up, up, yes. Is it okay, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But I would kindly ask the witness to memorise this. And when we zoom out, can you see Vitkovac now and the TV building?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we go back, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark Vitkovac and the TV building in this map?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Vitkovac, number 1; is that what you did?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: TV building, please put number 2. Or if you agree that it corresponds to number 17, we don't need any marks.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It corresponds to 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now mark the place from which the projectile was fired?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Today, I then have to make an area marked, Ilidza area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Okay, please go ahead. Mark this area.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put number 2.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This point of origin of fire was on which riverbank?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you draw a trajectory between position number 17 and the position from which the projectile was fired?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that with number 3?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now mark the PTT building in this map? Is it a little bit north of number 15?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mark the PTT building [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we put number 4, please?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that this trajectory was pretty much a horizontal one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the proceedings against General Milosevic, Judge Robinson asked you about the shape of the trajectory, and you said that it was horizontal, pretty horizontal. And if that were the case, it should have impacted the wall at a right angle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, if I have said that it was pretty horizontal, I was comparing it with an artillery or a mortar trajectory or path, and it's flatter or more horizontal because -- I can't find the right English word. It's not that ballistic that -- an artillery or mortar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to draw attention to the parties to page 3466 of the 8th of March, 2005, and then we can see what was it that you said exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have it in e-court? But let's keep this, first of all. Could you put the date of today and your signature on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it's already November. Yes, we'll give the number for this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is Exhibit D851.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. Do we have it in e-court; I mean, the transcript of the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just see what the number is. I think it was offered by the OTP as 65 ter 10249. And then we need page 10249 -- no, no, that's the number of this thing, but it says here "3466." So 3466 in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can see your response, which begins: "I understand ..." Would you be so kind as to read your reply.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to see what I'm -- what this answer is, because I think this is from -- I was --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brennskag, what was the shape of the trajectory or the path of this projectile?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not ballistic, but it was more -- because of the rocket that brought it out of the ballistic path, it was a little bit more - what do you call it? - horizontal than if it has been a ballistic missile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is exactly what I asked you about. So it was more horizontal than any other projectile; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the distance the ballistic projectiles are fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this particular projectile had a more horizontal trajectory than any other projectile fired from the same distance?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that, because I was not able to follow any other types of projectile in the air, the path, let's say, from artillery or from mortars, because they don't have any smoke tail you can trace in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then on the basis of what did you conclude this trajectory to be horizontal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like to read from the previous page, Mr. Brennskag?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure what the question was on this, so I must look a little bit before this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go one page further, and then we'll get back to this question. Actually, back. 3464, two pages back. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the question you were being asked, and you said that it was going towards PTT building: [In English] "And I saw the rocket smoke just afterwards, and impact in the TV building." [Interpretation] Judge Harhoff asked you: "And was it a straight line from the launching point to the impact point?" And you said: "Yes." And then Judge Harhoff asked you the following: "So the implication of your answer is that the modified air-bomb that you saw --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Scroll down. Let the witness read the transcript. If you're done --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know what I was answering, because I was asked to point out from where the firing point should be if Mr. Hansen's report was correct, and I marked it on the map. And then I was asked if it was fired from that point to the PTT building, it would be a horizontal trajectory, and that's also I said it would be a big problem to fire a modified air-bomb from that place. That's why I said, in my statement on the board here now, that it must be then horizontal. Am I clarifying it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then Judge Harhoff asked you if your response implied that the modified air-bomb could not have passed over the point identified by Captain Hansen, is that correct, and you answered, Yes; is that correct? It's on the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, then I go back to the report from Captain Hansen. And if his report is correct, the projectile couldn't pass, as far as I know, just across the PTT building, where the UN observers had their HQ. And that's my answer, because where I was asked to -- to tell where Captain Hansen was -- Captain Hansen said the modified air-bomb was fired from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll go back to the map shortly. Now, you said if the trajectory was horizontal, for it to go off, it needed to impact a wall at an angle of 90 degrees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's again from -- if Captain Hansen's report is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But in the case cited by you, saying that the trajectory was horizontal, what would then happen had this projectile hit a flat roof? Would it go off or would it ricochet?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The modified air-bomb I observed and reported was not horizontal, but a little bit more horizontal than a ballistic missile, and I can't speculate in what happened where it impacted because I did not -- I was not at the spot and I did not investigate the impact in the TV building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you maintain your opinion that in order for the bomb to go off, its fuse should have impacted close to 90 degrees? A horizontal shot, in order to go off, must hit a wall at an angle close to 90 degrees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about that. I only said, in a previous statement, that if Captain Hansen's report of the origin of firing, the projectile had to be almost horizontal, and then if it was almost horizontal, it would have hit a wall almost 90 degrees to the wall.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have these two pages admitted into evidence? Can we go three pages further, back to 3466. And we would like to tender into evidence 3464, 3465, and 3466. Now, let's look again at your answer on page 3466.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's admit from 3463 to 66, four pages, in order to understand the context.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D852, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at it. And tell me, is this your answer at line 15 which begins: "I understand"; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the line, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have the previous map back again, the one with the markings, P851.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was Captain Hansen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have to raise it right now. Given that the same team is working for the whole of today, there's an amount of time that we can sit altogether for today. If we are going to go further than 12.30 today in the morning, then the time for us to be able to sit for videolink will be limited, which means you have to spend more time tomorrow morning. So by 12.00, you will have spent almost three hours, which was originally allowed, so think about concluding your cross-examination by 12.30 or 25 in order for the Prosecution to have some redirect. I'll leave it in your hands. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll do my best, but I'm afraid that it will not be sufficient, once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brennskag, where was Captain Hansen at the time when this projectile flew over? Is it true that he was in the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: This will be second-hand information. So I don't know exactly, but I think he was inside the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the direction quoted in his report by Captain Hansen? Was that north-west?

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you please draw the north-west trajectory in this map? And after that, we shall look at his document.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid this is south-easterly direction. That's what you marked --

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is north-west.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- do you agree? But the shell that he is talking about, according to him, came from north-west to south-east. It came from north-west; it didn't go to that direction.

utterances.speaker: PER ANTON BRENNSKAG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misunderstood. I pointed out the north-west direction on the map. And if he said it would be like this, this is south-east/north-west [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please draw this line with respect to the point of impact in the TV building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we all know where the north is. Is it necessary?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is necessary because the trajectory that would have come from north-west would go exactly over the PTT building, where Captain Hansen and his fellow officer were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. We'll delete that direction first, north-west. Delete. And then if you could draw a line that would come to that PTT building from the north-west direction. Shall we draw it in red, in the red colour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You said "PTT building"?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] TV building, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The TV building.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you can put number 5 to indicate the direction quoted by Captain Hansen. Maybe we can tender it under the same number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we can keep it as it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By all respect, I don't remember -- I don't know Captain Hansen's statement right now, so I mark only the arrow that points from north-west to south-east across the TV building and mark it with -- which number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Number 5. Thank you, Mr. Brennskag.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 9837. 9837, 65 ter.
